explanations.answer: Remembering him and keeping the traditions he passed on
explanations.explanation: Yes, baker. Paul says, “Now I commend you for remembering me in everything and for maintaining the traditions, just as I passed them on to you.” That's a double compliment: they remembered him, and they kept what he handed down. If somebody told me I was remembered in EVERYTHING, I'd need to sit down on this gold base for a minute.

explanations.answer: Sending gifts to help with his travels
explanations.explanation: Not in this verse, friend. Gifts never come up here. Paul commends them for “…remembering me in everything and for maintaining the traditions, just as I passed them on to you.” So the praise is about remembering him and keeping what he taught.

explanations.answer: Ending all the quarrels among them
explanations.explanation: Quarrels don't come up in this verse. Paul's compliment is about two things: they remember him in everything, and they maintain the traditions just as he passed them on. Nothing in his words here says anything about arguments. This is a plain, warm thank-you, so take it as one.

That's the one. Paul says, “…the head of every man is Christ, and the head of the woman is man…” So Christ is the head named for every man. Notice he's laying out a line of heads here, and he's about to add one more.

Moses was Israel's leader, a giant of a name, but Paul never mentions him in this verse. He says, “…the head of every man is Christ…” That's the name that fills the blank. Easy to grab a famous name when you're in a hurry, baker. I've grabbed the wrong cookie cutter in a hurry, too.
Abraham is an ancestor of Israel, but he's not in this verse at all. Paul says, “…the head of every man is Christ…” So the blank is Christ. Paul names the heads here, and Abraham isn't one of them.
Right on the money. Paul finishes the list with “…the head of Christ is God.” That's the last of the three heads he names, and it's God. I like how he lines them up so clearly, step by step.
The church isn't one of the heads Paul lists. He names three: Christ for every man, man for the woman, and God for Christ. His words are “…the head of Christ is God.” So the answer is God.
The apostles don't show up in this list. Paul says, “…the head of Christ is God.” That's the whole answer, no committee needed. Three heads, and the apostles aren't among them.

That's what Paul says: “Every man who prays or prophesies with his head covered dishonors his head.” The word is dishonors, so keep your eye on it. This verse is about a man who prays or prophesies with his head covered. Paul states it plainly, and so do I.

Humility is a nice word, but it's not Paul's word here. He says, “Every man who prays or prophesies with his head covered dishonors his head.” Dishonors is what he says. Sometimes a nice-sounding answer is just a cookie that looks good on the cooling rack.
Elders don't come up in this verse. Paul says a man who prays or prophesies with his head covered “…dishonors his head.” The verse is about the man and his head. No elders in sight.

Close, but Paul says the opposite. He says, “And every woman who prays or prophesies with her head uncovered dishonors her head…” The word is dishonors, not honors. That one little word flips the whole statement, baker.

Yes, this one is false. Paul says a woman who prays or prophesies with her head uncovered “…dishonors her head…” The word is dishonors. Spotting the flipped word on a card like this takes a sharp eye, and you've got one.
That's it. Paul says, “…she should cover her head.” It comes right after he says that if it's shameful for a woman to have her hair cut or shaved off. The word is cover, plain and simple.
Lift isn't Paul's word. He says, “…she should cover her head.” The blank is cover. Nothing in this verse is about lifting anything.
Bowing isn't in this verse. Paul says, “…she should cover her head.” So the blank is cover. Bowing sounds like it fits a prayer, I'll give you that.

explanations.answer: He is the image and glory of God
explanations.explanation: You've got it. Paul says, “A man ought not to cover his head, since he is the image and glory of God…” Image and glory of God is the reason he gives. Then he moves on to the woman, so stay with me.

explanations.answer: He leads the prayers out loud
explanations.explanation: Paul doesn't say that. His reason is that a man “…is the image and glory of God…” Nothing in this verse is about who leads the prayers. When Paul gives a reason, I stick to the reason he gave.

explanations.answer: He was the first to be baptized
explanations.explanation: Baptism doesn't come up in this verse. Paul says, “A man ought not to cover his head, since he is the image and glory of God…” That's the reason he gives. It's right there in his words.
True! Paul says, “For man did not come from woman, but woman from man.” That's his reason for what he just said about the woman being the glory of man. Short verse, clear answer.

Paul actually says the reverse of the false option. He says, “For man did not come from woman, but woman from man.” So woman came from man, and the statement is true. It's easy to flip these around on a quick read, baker.

That's right. Paul says, “For this reason a woman ought to have a sign of authority on her head, because of the angels.” The phrase is “because of the angels.” He doesn't explain it further in these verses, so I won't either.
Elders aren't named here. Paul says a woman ought to have a sign of authority on her head “…because of the angels.” That's the answer. The verse names angels and nobody else.

Prophets don't appear in this verse. Paul says the sign of authority is “…because of the angels.” Prophesying comes up in the passage, but the prophets aren't the ones named here. The answer is the angels.

True. Paul says, “In the Lord, however, woman is not independent of man, nor is man independent of woman.” It goes both ways, and Paul says so himself. That little word “however” turns the corner for him.

This statement is actually true, baker. Paul says, “In the Lord, however, woman is not independent of man, nor is man independent of woman.” Neither one is independent of the other. It's easy to second-guess a true one when the verses before it were so heavy.

Correct. Paul says, “For just as woman came from man, so also man is born of woman.” So it goes in both directions, and that matches what he said right before. Then he adds that everything comes from God.

explanations.answer: He is formed from the dust
explanations.explanation: Genesis 2:7 does tell of God forming the first man from the dust of the ground, but that's not what Paul says here. He says, “…so also man is born of woman.” So the answer is born of woman. Same Bible, different verse.

explanations.answer: He is born of the Spirit
explanations.explanation: That's not what Paul says in this verse. He says, “…so also man is born of woman.” The answer is born of woman. Stick with Paul's words and you'll be fine.
That's it. Paul says, “Judge for yourselves: Is it proper for a woman to pray to God with her head uncovered?” The command comes first, and then the question. He hands it to them to weigh.
Not before the question. Paul says, “Judge for yourselves…” The other churches only come up at the very end, in verse 16. Right before he asks, the instruction is to judge for themselves.
Paul doesn't say that in these verses. Right before the question, he says, “Judge for yourselves…” He asks them to weigh it themselves. There's no waiting in this verse.

Almost, but Paul says the opposite about the man. He asks, “Doesn’t nature itself teach you that if a man has long hair, it is a disgrace to him…” So for a man, long hair is a disgrace. The glory goes to the woman, as he says next: “…if a woman has long hair, it is her glory?”

Yes, this one is false. Paul asks if nature teaches that “…if a man has long hair, it is a disgrace to him…” The glory belongs to the woman, he says: “…if a woman has long hair, it is her glory?” The card swapped them, and you caught it.
Yes, covering. Paul says, “For long hair is given to her as a covering.” That's the reason he gives for calling it her glory. He ties it all together in that one word.
Crown is a fine word, but Paul doesn't use it here. He says, “For long hair is given to her as a covering.” The blank is covering. It would sound fancy as a crown, I'll give you that.
Reward isn't Paul's word in this verse. He says, “For long hair is given to her as a covering.” So the blank is covering. The verse is about what the hair is given as.

explanations.answer: We and the churches of God have no other practice
explanations.explanation: That's what Paul says. He writes, “If anyone is inclined to dispute this, we have no other practice, nor do the churches of God.” He points to what he and the churches of God do. It's his closing word on the whole subject.

explanations.answer: Each church may choose its own way to do this
explanations.explanation: That's not what Paul says. He says, “…we have no other practice, nor do the churches of God.” No other practice means just that. The verse doesn't offer a choice.

explanations.answer: Bring it to the apostles and elders in Jerusalem
explanations.explanation: Paul doesn't send anyone to Jerusalem in this verse. He says, “If anyone is inclined to dispute this, we have no other practice, nor do the churches of God.” That's the whole reply. Nobody has to pack a bag.
